html:
The Cahora Bassa Dam on the Zambezi in Tete province, Mozambique, was built by Portugal between 1969 and 1974 and is one of the largest hydroelectric dams in Africa.

Portugal built it during the war of independence, hoping it would bring white settlers to the valley, and sold most of its power to South Africa through long transmission lines. FRELIMO attacked the building works.

Portugal kept control of the company after independence, and RENAMO cut the power lines in the civil war. Mozambique took majority control in 2007. The dam's lake drowned the valley of the old prazos, and its control of floods changed life downstream on the Zambezi.
sum: The Cahora Bassa Dam on the Zambezi in Tete province, Mozambique, was built by Portugal between 1969 and 1974 and is one of the largest hydroelectric dams in Africa.
